title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: The time seems long since I saw thee or received a line from thee. Last gave account of your setting out to see us, which would have been very agreeable. It was a favor you were not hurt, the last account from you was your being in town and to see the doctor, and that thee had a prospect of coming again to have something done to James’s throat, which has caused some anxiety of mind amongst us. We are very desirous of having a particular account from you, hoping you may be directed to do for the best. The intelligence of our dear friend Joseph Potts’s death was affecting, and strikingly shows us the necessity of being also ready. Our ancient neighbor Elizabeth Lippincott was buried yesterday who departed very suddenly. Also Hendal Coat and several others of the elder class hath dropped off here and here a ways of late. William Bundle and wife of Burlington were both buried together in one grave though he died a week first. it is said the old must go and the young may and often does, and it most assuredly behooves us of every class to be diligent and endeavoring to have our accounts in readiness against the great and awful day of judgment, which is hastening on.

We are through favor enjoying better health than for some time past. Lydia has been quite poorly with a colic complaint, but is now much better and hath passed one meeting, which probably thee may have heard of. We have and are like to have our engagements, and if health and convenience will admit of thine and James’s company at the time of Joshua and Lydia’s accomplishing their intentions–which I rather expect will be the next week after the monthly–if nothing unexpectedly prevents. I wish thee to think of it, and if way opens your company is very desirable.

closer.salute: Not having much more to communicate at present I conclude with near love in which my Husband and Lydia unites to you all, and am thy sympathizing Mother,
